Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
Persistent fever with alternating chills/sweats, myalgias, nausea and fatigue for 7 days in a 30-year-old nurse. No localizing infectious focus on review of systems. Returned from rural Vietnam 4 weeks ago with extensive outdoor exposure; took daily malaria prophylaxis (drug unknown).  
Differential (consistent with DDx):  
• Malaria – high likelihood given travel, cyclic hot/cold pattern, sweats.  
• Acute systemic viral illness (e.g., influenza/COVID-19) – moderate likelihood.  
• Dengue/other arboviral infection – lower likelihood but considered due to travel.  
Plan: Arrange urgent in-person assessment at central London clinic (or local ED) for physical examination. Order malaria thick/thin blood films, full blood count, inflammatory markers and other baseline labs per examiner judgment. Patient advised not to work until evaluated. Clinician to document plan and contact details; administrative team to book same-day appointment.

Management Plan
-  Urgent face-to-face review today; if travel to clinic impossible, attend local A&E  
-  Blood tests: malaria films, FBC, inflammatory markers; additional tests per examiner  
-  Provide consultation note for reception to expedite testing  
-  Off-work advice until diagnosis and treatment plan established  
-  Safety-netting: seek immediate care for worsening symptoms, rigors, confusion, rash, or shortness of breath  

Consider:
- Pathology tests as above:  Consider additional serology (dengue, typhoid) and renal/liver profile – to be decided after exam

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Malaria – High likelihood: compatible travel history, fever with chills/sweats, myalgias; prophylaxis not fully protective.  
2. Acute systemic viral infection (e.g., influenza/COVID-19) – Moderate likelihood: nonspecific viral syndrome; no focal signs.  
3. Dengue/arboviral infection – Low-moderate likelihood: endemic area exposure; absence of typical rash/arthralgia decreases probability.
